How this list is built

Checked

At the source

Every ride was confirmed where its host posts it: a club site, a shop calendar, a city program. Every card says when.

Dated

Newest check Sep 30, 2026

A ride we can't re-confirm within 150 days comes off the list on its own. Its page stays up and says why.

Flagged

30 marked Unconfirmed

Found on one source, or a detail we couldn't pin down. The card tells you to confirm first.

Free

No paid placement

Nobody pays to be listed or to rank. Tell us when a ride is gone, changed, or still on.

The ones people ask first

What's a no-drop ride?

The group waits for the slowest rider. If you come off the back on a hill, someone regroups with you. If it's your first group ride, start with one of these.

Do I need a road bike?

No. Social rides and slow rolls take whatever bike you have. Road rides are easier on a road bike. Gravel and mountain bike rides need the tires for it. Every ride page says which bike it's for.

What do I bring?

A helmet, water, a spare tube or patch kit, lights if it ends after dark, and a card for the coffee stop. Every ride page has a first-time checklist.

What if I can't keep up?

Tell the leader you're new before you roll. Pick a no-drop or beginner-friendly ride the first time. If a drop ride leaves you, you ride home at your own pace. Nobody minds.

Free to list

Run a ride? Add it, or fix what we got wrong.

Tell us what's new or what changed. We check it against the ride's own page before it goes up. Listing is free and always will be.

What is this about?

Why Cycle for Change keeps a group ride directory

A group ride is the cheapest, most reliable way I know to get out of my own head and into a room of people who want you there. Nobody asks what you do. You just ride. In 2027 I’m riding 10,000 miles for queer communities, and a lot of them will be on rides like these. This directory exists so anyone, anywhere, can find one this week.

If you're struggling: the 988 Suicide & Crisis Lifeline is free and 24/7 — call or text 988. For LGBTQ youth, the Trevor Project is at 1-866-488-7386 (or text START to 678-678).

10000

I do the miles. You decide who they’re for.

In 2027 I ride 10,000 miles, all on the bike, every one of them for queer communities. You pledge a few cents a mile and vote where the money goes. It starts January 1.
